facts.text: We'll make do with what we have. Eat, Jim, then go earn some more.
facts.why: Set out as Mae's rules in her own words, but it is not a line from the film. Mae dreads the fights and hates the idea of Jim going back to the ring, so 'go earn some more' is against her character. A real Mae line from the quotes page is 'Every time you get hit, feels like I'm getting hit too.'
facts.fix: Every time you get hit, feels like I'm getting hit too.

fix_note.text: Every time you get hit, feels like I'm getting hit too.

facts.text: Joe Gould's round after the Baer fight.
facts.why: No scene shows Gould buying a round. The film ends on Braddock beating Max Baer and winning the heavyweight title, so a toast to the new champ is what holds up.
facts.fix: A toast to the new champ after the Baer fight.

facts.text: The first proper meal after a win.
facts.why: No meal after a win is shown. The steak that is shown is the thick, juicy one Jim dreams about at the breakfast table in the opening scene.
facts.fix: the thick, juicy steak Jim dreams about

facts.text: Jim skips his and gives Rosy his share.
facts.why: At the table Rosy asks for more, and Jim describes a dream feast, says he is stuffed and asks the kids to give him a hand finishing his plate.

vibe.verdict: The Braddock kitchen table recipe box suits the Depression setting, with relief bread and dripping, the Baer fight list and Mae's line.
